text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST

- Appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney general met with protest by cabinet ministers who say they don't know anything about him and criticise Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to give them a week to find out about him.
- Analysis: Bar-On will toe Netanyahu's line.
- Hizbollah, Hamas groups vow fresh attacks.
- U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross: No agreement on broad pullback.
- Palestinian Authority says it will punish Ramadan offenders.
HAARETZ
- Heavy criticism in political and legal establishment of Bar-On's appointment as attorney general.

- Egyptian Ambassador Mohammed Bassiouny tells ultra-Orthodox newspaper Hashavua: The agreement between Israel and Egypt will break if Israel won't sign agreement with Syria. Israel will permit transfer of 80 Palestinian families from Rafah in Egypt to Rafah in Gaza.
- Israel tries to thwart Palestinian programme to set up a tourist area next to Gush Katif.
- Significant rise in number of school trips to West Bank.
- Silver gift from Netanyahu to Greek Orthodox archbishop shows Jerusalem without the Moslem holy sites, depicts the Temple in place of al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock.
- Privatisation plan will be put to ministerial committee vote on Monday: Israel Chemicals, Bezeq and Zim the main companies up for sale.
MAARIV
- The Hebron agreement: The Tomb of the Patriarchs problem to be put off for three months. Deal would be carried out within 10 days from signing. Two joint patrols in Hebron.
- Deputy director-general of prime minister's office says there are conversations between the prime minister's office and Bank of Israel to lower the interest rate.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Invitation from world fencing headquarters in Paris sent on official Iranian stationery inviting the Israeli team to participate in competition in Tehran in February.
